lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: simulation and model limitations

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 5 options and one side dish from 6 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 4-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 37 times in 148 spins. A simulation of 148 spins landed on that section 30 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: An event has a probability of 9/10. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 20 times and landed on blue 10 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
A bag has 3 red, 5 blue, and 10 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 4 equal sections numbered 1 to 4 is spun. What is the probability of getting tails on the coin and landing on 2 on the spinner?
A meal is made by choosing one main dish from 2 options and one side dish from 3 options. How many different meals are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 8-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 28 times in 224 spins. A simulation of 224 spins landed on that section 30 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: An event has a probability of 1. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 40 times and landed on blue 17 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
